answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked reputation escrow: every new identity must lock a bond that vests only after many epochs of verified honest work, like a violet thread slowly weaving through a nebula of attestations. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund thousands of bonds and wait out the vesting clock for each, while honest agents earn their bond back plus rewards. Early misbehavior slashes the bond, so creating fake identities costs real capital and real time, far more than the rewards a Sybil swarm can extract before detection.
